reader.notes: The transfer is one 80-character record (DOC-A.1-5); AcceptSource.Device appends records until the receiver's size and cuts at that size, which is GR4a's left-aligned fill with more data requested and GR4b's truncation. The run helper starts the program with a null standard input, so the input-bearing runs compiled through run_probe.py --compile-only in a fresh directory and ran the produced dll there with the .in file redirected. 'In level 1, only one transfer' does not bind: the implementation provides the level-2 Nucleus.

refuter.evidence: Probe r1comp (runs/r1comp-001 at --std 85, r1comp-002 at --std 2023; compiled with run_probe.py --compile-only, the dll run in that fresh directory with src/r1comp.in redirected): input line '12345678' into PIC 9(4) DISPLAY, COMP, BINARY and PACKED-DECIMAL printed 'D4[1234] C4[5678] B4[5678] K4[5678]'; input '12.50CR' into PIC 9(3)V99 COMP and DISPLAY printed 'CV[000.00] DV[012.50]'. Identical at --std 2023. The 1985 size of every one of these receivers is 4 (resp. 5) characters: cite.py 'OK  §1985:IV.4.3.4  (4.3.4 Selection of Character Representation and Radix)  the text is in the clause' for 'The size of an elementary data item or a group item is the number of characters in standard data format of the item. Synchronization and usage may cause a difference between this size and that required for internal representation'. The 80-character transfer exceeds that size, so GR4b keeps the leftmost characters and ignores the rest: cite.py 'OK  §1985:VI.6.5.4 GR4b ... the text is in GR4b' for 'only the leftmost characters of the transferred data are stored in the receiving data item' and 'OK  §1985:VI.6.5.4 GR4' for 'The remaining characters of the transferred data which do not fit into the receiving data item are ignored'. A binary or packed receiver instead takes ONE WHOLE RECORD (AcceptSource.DeviceNumeric: Device(receiver.ByteForm == Zoned ? size : RecordSize)) and converts all of it, so characters 5-8 decide the value (5678) and the 'CR' past the fifth position makes the value zero: characters GR4b says are ignored are examined. The implementor's own size statement agrees with GR4b and not with the code: DOC-A.1-5 gives the receiving size GR3/GR4 compare against as 'the digit count plus a SIGN SEPARATE position for a fixed-point numeric one' and exempts only floating-point (one record); DOC-A.1-1 documents the whole-record read for binary/packed, so the two implementor entries contradict each other. GR1's implementor conversion governs how the stored characters become the item's representation, not which characters are stored; USAGE COMPUTATIONAL's implementor latitude (§1985:VI.5.14.4 GR4, checked OK) covers representation and range, not the standard-data-format size. Other probes upheld the reader: r1acc-001 (JUSTIFIED RIGHT X(5) from 'AB' -> [AB   ], 9(5) from '1234567' -> [12345], X(85) from 'A' then 'BCDEFGH' -> A + 79 spaces + BCDEF, A(3) from 'XYZW' -> [XYZ], X(100) from a 120-character line -> its first 100, group with a JUSTIFIED RIGHT member from 'P' -> [P ][  ]); class c r1endacc-001: 'ACCEPT X1 END-ACCEPT' refused at 85, COBOL0816.

refuter.corrected: NON-CONFORMING (wrong-answer, silent), cause (b): the same at --std 2023. Minimal repro: 01 C4 PIC 9(4) COMP. ACCEPT C4. DISPLAY C4. with input '12345678' prints 5678; §1985:VI.6.5.4 GR4b with the 1985 size of the item (4 characters, §1985:IV.4.3.4) stores the leftmost four characters, '1234', and ignores the rest, as the same program does for PIC 9(4) DISPLAY (1234). '12.50CR' into PIC 9(3)V99 COMP stores zero where the five-character window '12.50' is 12.50. Known: kb/Work PB3513 (landed) chose the whole-record read for binary/packed deliberately, following GnuCOBOL 3.2.0, as GR1 conversion latitude; that latitude does not reach GR4b's choice of which characters are stored, and DOC-A.1-5 states the opposite size. Reading stated: if the owner holds that a binary item's GR4 size is one record, DOC-A.1-5 must say so and this becomes a documentation defect only.
